cases.description: No analyses at all: the rank is null, never a fabricated Bronze.
Only low_confidence rows (score null): nothing countable remains, so the rank is null.
A newer low_confidence row beside one scored analysis changes nothing: only the scored row counts, and it is the technique's latest capture.
One scored dink at 6.3: technique score equals the raw score, rating equals the technique score, Gold I (6.3 is above 2/3 of the 5-6.5 band).
Rows without a `source` field (mobile RealAnalysisFact shape) count as real evidence.
The previous case with its rows shuffled; the summary is identical.
Ten dinks scored 1..10 by day: only the newest eight (3..10) define form with weights 8..1, but all ten count as evidence.
Two dinks at the same instant: the higher id is 'newest' (weight 8), the lower id gets weight 7.
Ids are compared as lowercase uuid text (Postgres uuid byte order): 'F…' outranks 'e…' even though 'F' < 'e' in raw string order.
6.005 and 2.345 quantize to hundredths on their decimal text (half away from zero, as numeric(4,2) stores them): 6.01 and 2.35, rating 4.18.
Two techniques with one analysis each at 5.00 and 5.01: (500+501)/2 = 500.5 → 5.01.
Seven dinks at 7.0 and one serve at 7.0: technique weights are min(count,5)=5 and 1; the rating is 7.00 regardless.
Three techniques at 6.2: listed alphabetically by shot type when scores tie.
A score of exactly 0 is countable evidence: Bronze III with the full 3.5 points to Silver.
A rating of exactly 3.5 is Silver (tier floors are inclusive), division III.
Gold band is 5-6.5; 5.5 sits exactly on the 1/3 mark → division II.
Gold band is 5-6.5; 6.0 sits exactly on the 2/3 mark → division I.
A rating of exactly 7.5 is Diamond III with nextTier null.
A perfect 10 is Diamond I.
Two drives inside one millisecond: SQL keeps timestamptz microseconds, so the .000900 row is newer than .000001 (weights 8 and 7), with a newer millisecond row on top as the reported capture.
Seven-digit fractions .0000015 and .0000024 both round to microsecond 2 (rint), so the rows share an instant and id descending decides recency; a newer whole-millisecond row is the reported capture.
Mixed-case and punctuated shot types at one score list in UTF-16 code-unit order (uppercase before underscore before lowercase), as GET /v1/rank orders them — never a locale collation.

A nine-digit fraction (the ingress maximum) is a valid capture; timestamptz rounds it to .123457, one microsecond newer than the .123456 row, so it takes weight 7 behind the newer whole-millisecond row.

replays.description: One id arrives three times with different content, earliest capture first. The first storable arrival (drive 9) is the analysis; the two later copies are replays the server acknowledges without reading, so they never count. Another arrival order gives another rating (see the late-capture-first case).

The same conflicting id as above, but the later capture (drive 3) arrives first and therefore holds the id on every plane: SQL stores it and shots_pkey refuses the earlier capture; TS keeps the first storable arrival. Rating differs from capture-order arrival by design.
Byte-identical replays of two ids (one copy spelt with an uppercase uuid) count once each; every permutation reproduces this summary on every plane.

A low_confidence row is storable: it holds its id and contributes nothing, so a scored copy of the same id arriving behind it is a replay and never counts. Nothing scored remains, so the rank is null, not a fabricated Bronze.

A row no plane stores (score above the scale) does not hold its id: the in-domain copy arriving behind it is the analysis on every plane, and the differing copy behind that one is a replay (so arrival order among the stored copies matters, as on the server).

rejectedInputs.description: An unrecognised resultKind never counts.
A low_confidence row carrying a numeric score is still an abstention: resultKind decides, not the score.
A scored row with a null score has no evidence to count.
10.5 is outside the 0-10 domain.
-0.1 is outside the 0-10 domain.
An empty shot type identifies no technique.
A whitespace-only shot type identifies no technique.
A shot type longer than 64 characters is refused.
Fixture output must never enter user history or rank a player.
Capture instants before 2000-01-01 are outside the storable range.
Capture instants from 2100-01-01 on are outside the storable range.
Text that is not an instant has no recency and cannot be stored.
A local-time instant (no Z) is outside the ingress grammar; SQL would read it in the session zone, not as the device meant it.
A zone offset is outside the ingress grammar even though it names an instant.
February 30 matches the grammar but is not a calendar date; the ingress round-trips the fields and refuses it.
Ten fractional digits exceed the ingress grammar (1-9).
33 emoji are 66 UTF-16 code units: over the 64 cap the ingress measures with String#length, though only 33 code points.

Postgres text cannot hold U+0000: the wire refuses the row (sqlstate 22021) whichever route it takes, while the Edge parser admits it. TS excludes it so the device never counts what the account plane can never store.

1999-12-31T23:59:59.9999995Z stores as 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z (half-even microseconds) so the SQL bounds check admits it, but the Edge parser compares Date.parse milliseconds (…59.999) and refuses it. TS excludes it because not every plane's check admits it.

2099-12-31T23:59:59.9999995Z is inside 2099 at millisecond precision, so the Edge parser admits it, but it stores as 2100-01-01T00:00:00Z and shots_captured_at_bounds refuses it. TS excludes it because not every plane's check admits it.
